Zoho Inventory keeps the records it holds today: Your customer records, stock, batch history and invoices live there. What we hold is every kitchen's order guide with its prices, kept current by you, along with the orders kitchens place in our app.

The portal carries on for invoices and payments: Restaurants keep looking up orders and paying bills there, as they do now. The app is only where an order starts. A call to your office still gets no number from us; only app orders get one.
A Zoho Commerce store can stay for accounts that browse: If you run one, keep it: some accounts like to search a catalog and type. The app is for the chef who finds it quicker to talk than to search.

@graph.name: From a Zoho export to the first app order
@graph.description: It starts with a file you already have. We build the guides from it, and each restaurant can begin ordering in the app.

step.name: Export your customers' items
step.text: The price list or item export Zoho already produces, saved as Excel or CSV, is usually all we need.

step.name: We open each kitchen's account
step.text: We load its guide and set the account up, and the kitchen installs the app. Most place a first order the same day.

step.name: Orders land in the format you picked
step.text: Each one has been checked by the chef, item by item, and carries a number and a time.

@graph.name: Do we need a Zoho Inventory alternative before kitchens can order on their own?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your stock stays in Zoho, and its portal keeps handling bills and payments. The one thing the portal will not do is accept an order from the restaurant. Our app fills that gap: a chef tells it what is short, checks the items and sends them.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Zoho Inventory?

acceptedAnswer.text: For one job, yes: the order Zoho's portal cannot take, sent by a chef who would otherwise call, with every item checked first. We do not set out to be a Zoho Inventory replacement. Zoho Inventory does far more, from batches and warehouses to invoices, so the app goes beside it, not in its place.

@graph.name: Our kitchens already use the Zoho customer portal. Why not order there?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because Zoho built the portal for looking things up: its help pages list viewing sales orders, paying invoices and checking deliveries, and say customers cannot order there. Zoho's answer for online ordering is a separate product, Zoho Commerce. Keep the portal either way; the app only adds the order.

@graph.name: Does someone here still have to enter app orders into Zoho Inventory?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the format. Zoho and VoiceOrder Solutions are separate companies, nothing ties our app to Zoho, and each supports only its own software. EDI and API orders can land in Zoho with no retyping, provided your Zoho account is able to take them in; we check that with you in the demo. When you choose email, the order is a file (PDF, Word or Excel) that the chef reviewed before sending, and someone on your side enters it from there rather than from a call or a message left overnight.

@graph.name: Doesn't Zoho's own AI already create orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: Zoho's AI, Zia, answers questions about stock, orders and customers, and Zoho says AI agents can create orders through its tools. The voice links above are another route. Our app is a different thing: the chef voices the order, then checks each item from their own guide before it is sent.

@graph.name: Does setting this up change anything in our Zoho account?

acceptedAnswer.text: Getting started needs no Zoho login and installs nothing: we build from a file you pull out of Zoho, and your settings and pricing are left alone. If you later want orders to arrive by EDI or the API, the demo covers what that would take on your side.

@graph.name: How soon can we be live, and what does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most distributors are up and running in 24 to 48 hours. Zoho publishes its plan prices; ours is a quote for your business. Any Zoho Inventory alternative that takes over your stock means moving items, batches, warehouses and the accounting link in one go. Next to that move, adding one new way for restaurants to order is small.
